tldr: Two compounding shocks hit Thursday: widening Houthi drone attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure spiked Brent +3.7% to $112.80 and revived inflation/rate fears, which is the best explanation for why gold and silver sold off HARD instead of hedging (SLV -5.6%, GDX -5.8%, SILJ -6.5%, PAAS -7.3%) -- separately, Tesla's capex cut and Meta's AI-dilution share plan reignited AI-financing doubts, driving the VIX +9.9% to 19.03 and the Nasdaq -1.6%.

The silver-backed loan is now 17.6% away from a stressed margin call (per oneaction.json) -- today's miner-led rout is the most direct threat to the book's biggest single risk this run, and it is compounding rather than easing.

CORRECTION: the Hang Seng Index actually closed -3.03% at 22,934.68 Thursday, not the 23,867.74 this dashboard's automated feed showed (a two-session gap specific to the index symbol) -- the real HK tech picture is worse, driven by a fresh SAMR crackdown on Alibaba/JD.com/PDD over counterfeit-goods and quality-standard violations, layered on the standing Tencent/SMIC chip-control overhang.

Fed hold odds for the Oct 27-28 FOMC remain ~85-94%, but the residual tail has shifted toward a small HIKE, not a cut, as oil's rally builds the 'higher for longer' case -- a more hostile backdrop for both the SGX bank/REIT sleeve and the metals rout.

Treasuries rallied hard despite the equity selloff (10-year yield fell to ~4.96-4.97%, biggest one-day drop since March) -- a genuine safe-haven bid that didn't extend to gold, underscoring this was a liquidation of crowded positioning more than a classic flight-to-quality day.

Flows corroborate a broadening Asia-tech risk-off: Japan's foreign investors sold cash equities for the first time in 3 weeks, Korea saw foreigners and institutions both sell into a 3.5% KOSPI drop, and HK Southbound posted its deepest net sell of the current stretch (-HK$9.2bn).

regime.label: Oil-driven inflation scare plus an AI-capex financing wobble trigger a risk-off, metals-liquidation day
regime.oneLiner: Two distinct shocks -- Houthi attacks spiking oil/inflation fears, and reignited AI-capex-financing doubts -- compounded into a VIX spike and a sharp gold/silver liquidation, with Treasuries rallying but gold conspicuously failing to hedge.

topNews.headline: Hang Seng actually closed -3.03% at 22,934.68 Thursday -- worse than this dashboard's feed showed -- as Alibaba plunges on a China quality-standards crackdown
topNews.actionable: The true picture for HK tech going into Friday's open is notably worse than the feed showed; the SAMR e-commerce crackdown is a fresh, Alibaba-specific risk distinct from Tencent/SMIC's existing overhangs.

topNews.headline: Gold and silver miners lead a broad rout as Brent's surge above $110 revives rate-hike fears
topNews.actionable: The rout is an oil-driven inflation/rate scare, not a reversal of the physical silver-deficit thesis -- but miners trading as 'risk' first is exactly what hurts a levered miner sleeve hardest, and it is pushing the silver loan closer to its stressed margin call.

topNews.headline: Houthi drone campaign widens to Saudi Arabia's largest oilfield and King Fahd airport
topNews.actionable: A genuine, widening security escalation adding a real geopolitical risk premium to oil and, through it, to the inflation/rate-path narrative pressuring both the metals sleeve and SGX rate-sensitive names.

topNews.headline: VIX surges toward 19 as Tesla capex cut and Meta's AI share structure spook tech investors
topNews.actionable: A genuine re-escalation of the AI-capex-return doubt that has whipsawed the VIX multiple times this month -- reason to treat the cash pile's deployment decision as unresolved rather than lean into tech weakness as a clean dip.

topNews.headline: FOMC odds flip toward a small hike tail as hot inflation and oil-driven price pressure build into Oct 27-28
topNews.actionable: A hold is still the base case, but pricing a hike tail rather than a cut tail is a more hostile backdrop for both the SGX bank/REIT sleeve and the metals rout -- next Wednesday's statement is the clearest near-term catalyst for both.
